summary: Instagram is carrying almost all the attention: the Hindi videos get 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 30 views. The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner on both platforms, with the most views, likes, shares and saves. Street light and everyday-device questions do fine on Instagram, but the channel is still very small, so these results are early signals rather than proof.
winningPattern: Hindi explainer about a familiar everyday sensor that people meet daily (motion sensor, street light), with a curiosity hook that says a surprising fact or asks 'how does it know?' (e.g. 'Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'). Title is Hinglish, one short question, a 🤔 emoji and #shorts. Instagram Reels is the main driver; the PIR video was also the only one to get real YouTube traction.
doMore: Make videos about sensors people see every day (lights, doors, taps, alarms) and open with a surprising claim like 'It doesn't see you!'
Lead titles with the shocking statement, then the question, as the PIR title does
Post to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform, then repost to YouTube
Ask a question in each video that invites shares and saves, since shares and saves are what the best videos got
Keep to one sensor per video and revisit the PIR topic with a follow-up (e.g. PIR vs IR sensor)
stopDoing: Publishing near-duplicate topics like two smoke detector videos within days of each other
Mixing in English titles for now, since the Hindi videos are where the audience is
Abstract or internal topics (touchscreen, phone orientation) without a visible daily-life hook
nextTopics: Escalator that starts when you step near
Room light that turns on with a clap or motion
Fridge door light turning off when closed
